subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to relax stricter later global or agent exec security policy when a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally treat session exec fields as more-specific defaults, but the reported behavior can preserve a looser command-execution policy after an operator tightens configuration.

options.title: Clamp to current policy
options.body: Treat global, agent, and host-approval exec policy as the upper safety bound and clear or downgrade persisted session exec fields that exceed it, with upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistent session defaults
options.body: Document that `/exec` creates durable session defaults and require operators to reset sessions or run a repair flow after policy changes.

options.title: Ship reset tooling first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair path before changing the resolver semantics for existing persisted sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp to current policy
recommendation.body: Treat global, agent, and host-approval exec policy as the upper safety bound and clear or downgrade persisted session exec fields that exceed it, with upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the auto-reply `/exec` session override behavior and tests points to steipete.
